title: Special Executive Programme In International Marketing
description: The course aims to provide learners with a comprehensive understanding of international marketing strategies, environments, and trade dynamics.
longDescription: This course explores the nature and scope of international marketing, differentiating it from domestic marketing while introducing key marketing theories and trade concepts. Learners will examine international marketing environments, including legal, cultural, and political aspects, as well as consumer behavior in global contexts. Topics such as foreign market entry, distribution strategies, pricing, and the impact of trade barriers are covered to equip students with practical knowledge for navigating global markets.
courseDetails: International Legal Marketing Environment. International Cultural Marketing Environment. International Political Marketing environment. Understand Consumer Behaviour In The International Context. Understand Foreign Market Entry Strategies, Foreign Direct International. Appreciate Market Entry Strategy, Promotion and Pricing Strategies. Understand the Channels of Distribution. Learn about Physical Distribution and Documentation. Develop International Marketing Programme. Marketing barriers, such as tariff and non-tariff barriers. Understand the concept, role, and impact of protectionism. Explore the dynamics of different modes of transportation. Understand the importance and need for cargo or transportation insurance. Understand the role of freight forwarder and customs broker. Understand the working of the foreign exchange market and exchange rate systems. The course begins by exploring the foundational concepts of international marketing and trade theories, such as the theory of comparative advantage. Students will delve into the international marketing environment, focusing on the legal, cultural, and political factors influencing marketing decisions. Strategic topics like market entry strategies, pricing, distribution channels, and promotion in a global context will be covered, along with an analysis of trade barriers, protectionism, and the role of freight forwarders and customs brokers in international trade. After the successful completion of the course, the student will be able to learn the following: Nature and Scope of International Marketing International Marketing Environment Marketing Communication Strategy and Planning International Marketing Distribution Trade Distortions and Marketing Barriers

modules.title: International Marketing
modules.summary: International Marketing introduces students to the complexities of marketing beyond domestic boundaries. It covers trade theories, such as comparative advantage, and explores how legal, cultural, and political environments shape international marketing strategies. The course emphasizes foreign market entry, pricing, distribution, and promotional strategies while also addressing trade distortions and marketing barriers like tariffs and protectionism. Students will develop a global marketing program that navigates these challenges effectively.
